intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

selected_hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Japanese tradition of hanami (flower viewing) beneath hundreds of cherry blossom trees, including the famous weeping cherry tree illuminated at night. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the season, and capture breathtaking photos of pink blooms reflected in the park's pond. A quintessential family-friendly cultural experience.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Tokyo's legendary Tsukiji Outer Market and sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, and matcha treats from dozens of street vendors. A fantastic culinary adventure for families to taste authentic Japanese street food culture while wandering vibrant market stalls alongside local chefs and vendors.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: Visit the deeply moving Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and walk through the surrounding Peace Memorial Park, home to the iconic A-Bomb Dome. This profoundly educational experience offers families and history enthusiasts a powerful perspective on World War II and humanity's pursuit of peace. The museum is thoughtfully curated for visitors of all ages.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Tenryu-ji Temple
experiences.description: Walk through the enchanting towering bamboo groves of Arashiyama and explore the UNESCO-listed Tenryu-ji Temple with its stunning traditional Japanese garden featuring cherry blossom trees framing a serene koi pond. Rent a rickshaw for a family-friendly tour of the area and cross the historic Togetsukyo Bridge for panoramic mountain views.

experiences.name: Edo-Tokyo Museum Family Experience
experiences.description: Step back in time at the spectacular Edo-Tokyo Museum, where life-size reconstructions of historic Edo-period streets, bridges, and buildings bring Japanese history vividly to life. Families can interact with exhibits, try on traditional costumes, and learn about samurai culture, merchant life, and the transformation of Tokyo from ancient Edo. Highly engaging for children and adults alike.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Kansai International Airport at 13:00. Take the Haruka Express train to Kyoto Station (approx. 75 min, ~¥1,900). Check in to your boutique stay near Maruyama Park in the Gion district. Drop your luggage and take a gentle stroll through Maruyama Park to see the iconic weeping cherry blossom tree (Shidare-zakura), which should be in bloom in mid-April. The park is free to enter and is one of Kyoto's most beloved cherry blossom spots.
day_by_day.evening: Walk through the atmospheric stone-paved lanes of Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka, lined with traditional machiya townhouses, souvenir shops, and tea houses. Enjoy the lantern-lit ambiance of Gion's Hanamikoji Street and keep an eye out for geiko (geisha) heading to evening engagements.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a bento box or onigiri from a convenience store (7-Eleven, FamilyMart) at the airport or Kyoto Station (~¥400–¥700). Japan's convenience store food is genuinely excellent.
meals.dinner: Omen Noodle Restaurant near Gion — a beloved local spot serving hearty udon noodle sets for around ¥1,000–¥1,500. Alternatively, try a budget ramen shop near Shijo Street.

day_by_day.notes: IC card (Suica or ICOCA) is highly recommended — buy one at Kansai Airport for seamless train and bus travel. April mid-month is peak cherry blossom season, so Maruyama Park may be crowded but magical, especially at night (yozakura — night cherry blossoms). Keep your first evening light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine (free entry) — start by 7:00–8:00 AM to beat the crowds. Hike the iconic thousands of vermilion torii gates up the mountain trail. The lower section takes 30–45 minutes; the full hike to the summit and back is about 2–3 hours. The misty morning atmosphere among cherry trees and torii is spectacular. Take the JR Nara Line from Kyoto Station to Inari Station (2 stops, ~¥150).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Kyoto and visit Tofuku-ji Temple (garden entry ~¥500), known for its beautiful Zen garden and maple/cherry tree-lined ravine bridge (Tsutenkyo Bridge). Afterward, head to Nishiki Market — Kyoto's famous narrow covered food market nicknamed 'Kyoto's Kitchen.' Sample street foods like tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), pickled vegetables, and skewered tofu for ¥100–¥300 per item.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Pontocho Alley, a narrow lantern-lit dining lane running parallel to the Kamo River. In April, many restaurants open their riverside 'kawadoko' terraces. Watch the sunset over the Kamo River and join locals sitting along the riverbanks — a beloved Kyoto tradition.

meals.breakfast: Morning set (morning setto) at a local kissaten (coffee shop) near Gion — coffee + toast + egg for ~¥500–¥700. Or grab onigiri and green tea from a convenience store.
meals.lunch: Nishiki Market street food crawl — budget ¥600–¥1,000 for a satisfying variety of tastings.
meals.dinner: Pontocho area — look for standing sushi bars (tachinomi) or set-menu izakayas offering dinner sets from ¥800–¥1,500. Avoid the high-end kaiseki restaurants on this street; budget options are tucked between them.

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is about 20 minutes from Kyoto Station by JR — very accessible. Wear comfortable walking shoes as the torii gate path involves significant uphill walking. Nishiki Market closes early (most stalls by 6 PM), so visit in the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) — one of Japan's most iconic sights (entry ¥500). The gold-leaf-covered Zen temple reflected in the surrounding pond is breathtaking. Go early (opens at 9:00 AM) to beat tour groups. Afterward, walk to Ryoan-ji Temple (~15 min walk, entry ¥600) to contemplate Japan's most famous Zen rock garden — a UNESCO World Heritage site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Arashiyama district by bus or rental bicycle. Walk through the famous Bamboo Grove (free), visit Tenryu-ji Temple garden (¥500 garden entry, ¥800 including temple buildings), and stroll along the Oi River. The cherry blossoms along the Hozu River in Arashiyama are stunning in April. Rent a rowboat on the river for a peaceful experience (~¥1,500/hour for a small boat).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion area. Visit Yasaka Shrine (free, open 24 hours) adjacent to Maruyama Park — beautifully lit in the evening. Browse the Gion neighborhood and enjoy the traditional architecture.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel breakfast if included. Alternatively, try a local bakery near the hotel.
meals.lunch: Arashiyama area — Yoshida-ya tofu restaurant or a budget set lunch (teishoku) at a local restaurant for ¥800–¥1,200. Tofu cuisine is a Kyoto specialty and often affordable at local spots.
meals.dinner: Hirano-ya or a nearby izakaya in the Gion/Maruyama area. Try yakitori (grilled chicken skewers) at a local spot for ¥100–¥150 per skewer with a draft beer (~¥400).

day_by_day.notes: Saturday will be busy at all major sights. Arashiyama is best reached by the Sagano/San-in Line from Kyoto Station or by bus (¥230 flat fare with a day pass). Consider buying a Kyoto City Bus One-Day Pass (¥700) if visiting multiple bus-accessible sites — it pays for itself in 3 rides.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara (45 min from Kyoto by Kintetsu Express, ~¥680 one way). Visit Nara Park, where over 1,000 free-roaming sacred deer (shika) wander freely. Buy deer crackers (shika senbei, ¥200) for an unforgettable interactive experience — great for families! Walk to Todai-ji Temple (entry ¥600), home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue (Daibutsu), a truly awe-inspiring sight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kasuga Taisha Grand Shrine (free outer grounds, ¥500 for inner sanctuary) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its hundreds of stone and bronze lanterns. Walk through the forested Kasugayama Primeval Forest paths (free). Visit Kofuku-ji Temple pagoda (free exterior) and the nearby Nara National Museum if interested in Buddhist art (¥700).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening. Relax with an evening walk through Maruyama Park to enjoy the illuminated cherry blossoms (many Kyoto parks have yozakura illuminations in April). Stop at a konbini for snacks or a cold drink and join locals under the blossoms.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before departing for Nara.
meals.lunch: Nara — try kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf-wrapped sushi, a Nara specialty) from a local shop for ~¥800–¥1,000. Or grab a bento from a convenience store near Nara Station.
meals.dinner: Back in Kyoto — Ramen Kaikon near Shijo or any local ramen shop for a hearty bowl of ramen (~¥800–¥1,000). Ramen is the perfect budget comfort meal.

day_by_day.notes: The Kintetsu Nara Line is faster and cheaper than JR for reaching Nara from Kyoto. Nara Park is entirely walkable. Deer can be pushy when you have crackers — keep bags and food items secured, especially with young children. This is a fantastic family day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-Michi) — a 2 km stone path along a cherry-tree-lined canal in northern Kyoto, named after philosopher Nishida Kitaro who meditated here daily. In mid-April, the canal is carpeted with fallen cherry blossom petals (hanafubuki — 'flower blizzard'). Walk north to south, stopping at small shrines and cafes along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nanzen-ji Temple complex (free grounds, ¥500 for Sanmon Gate, ¥400 for Hojo garden) — one of Kyoto's most important Zen temples. Don't miss the surprisingly photogenic 19th-century brick aqueduct running through the temple grounds. Explore the sub-temples. Then visit Heian Jingu Shrine (free outer grounds, ¥600 for inner garden) with its large vermilion torii gate and beautiful strolling garden with cherry blossoms over ponds.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Kyoto Station area for shopping at the underground Porta Mall or the Isetan department store basement (depachika) — an affordable way to browse gourmet foods, sample free tastings, and pick up beautifully packaged Japanese snacks and sweets as souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a morning coffee and pastry at one of the charming small cafes along the Philosopher's Path (~¥500–¥800).
meals.lunch: Nanzen-ji area — try yudofu (tofu hot pot), a Kyoto specialty. Okutan Nanzen-ji offers a traditional yudofu set for ~¥3,000 (a splurge) or find a more affordable teishoku lunch set nearby for ¥900–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Kyoto Station area — Kyoto Ramen Koji on the 10th floor of the Kyoto Station building has 8 ramen restaurants with regional styles from across Japan, all in the ¥800–¥1,200 range. Fun and easy for families.

day_by_day.notes: The Philosopher's Path is best in the morning when the light is soft and crowds are thinner. Monday is typically less crowded at major temples than weekends. Wear comfortable shoes — today involves a lot of walking on varied terrain.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Osaka for the day (25 min from Kyoto by Shinkansen/JR Special Rapid, ~¥560 by regular JR). Visit Osaka Castle (Osaka-jo) — a magnificent reconstructed castle surrounded by a moat and cherry blossom trees. The park grounds are free; castle tower museum entry is ¥600. Climb to the top for panoramic city views. The surrounding park is one of Osaka's top hanami (cherry blossom viewing) spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Dotonbori, Osaka's famous entertainment and food district. Walk across the Dotonbori Bridge and see the iconic Glico Running Man sign. Explore Shinsaibashi shopping arcade (covered, free to walk) and Amerika-mura (American Village) for quirky youth fashion. Take a short Dotonbori canal boat cruise (~¥700–¥900) for a unique perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in Dotonbori sampling Osaka's legendary street food scene — the city is known as 'tenka no daidokoro' (the nation's kitchen). Try multiple stalls and restaurants before returning to Kyoto.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel before departing for Osaka.
meals.lunch: Osaka Castle area — convenience store bento or a nearby teishoku restaurant. Budget ¥600–¥1,000.
meals.dinner: Dotonbori street food feast: takoyaki (octopus balls, ¥500–¥600/8 pieces), okonomiyaki (savory pancake, ¥700–¥1,000), kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers, ¥100–¥200 each), and fresh crab claw if feeling slightly indulgent. Total budget: ¥1,500–¥2,500 for a very satisfying spread.

day_by_day.notes: Osaka is extremely easy to reach from Kyoto. The JR Special Rapid (kaisoku) on the JR Biwako/Kyoto Line is the cheapest option. Dotonbori is pedestrian-friendly and very family-friendly in the evening. Keep an eye on children in the busy crowds. Osaka's food is generally cheaper and more generous in portion than Kyoto.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Kiyomizu-dera Temple (entry ¥500) — one of Japan's most celebrated temples, built on a wooden stage jutting out from a hillside with sweeping views over Kyoto. The approach through Sannen-zaka and Ninen-zaka is lined with traditional shops. In April, cherry blossoms frame the temple beautifully. Go early (opens 6:00 AM) for the best light and fewer crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding Higashiyama district on foot. Visit Kodai-ji Temple (¥600) — a refined Zen temple with a bamboo grove, tea house, and beautiful garden. Walk through the Ishibei-koji lane, one of Kyoto's most atmospheric and photogenic stone-paved alleys. Browse artisan shops for handmade crafts, ceramics, and textiles — window shopping is free!
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free cultural experience: visit Yasaka Shrine (free) for evening prayers and atmosphere. If budget allows, consider booking a 1-hour traditional tea ceremony experience near Gion (many options from ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person, including matcha and wagashi sweets) — a meaningful cultural highlight, especially for families.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or a nearby cafe before heading to Kiyomizu-dera.
meals.lunch: Higashiyama area — try a kaiseki-style lunch set (lunch sets are significantly cheaper than dinner) at a local restaurant for ¥1,000–¥1,500. Or grab street snacks: mitarashi dango (rice dumplings with sweet soy sauce, ~¥150) and matcha soft serve (~¥400).
meals.dinner: Home-style Japanese cooking at a local family restaurant (famiresu) like Yayoi-ken near Gion — traditional Japanese set meals (teishoku) with rice, miso soup, and multiple small dishes for ¥700–¥1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Kiyomizu-dera is uphill from the main road — comfortable shoes essential. The temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The famous wooden stage ('kiyomizu no butai') is currently undergoing periodic maintenance phases — check current status. This area is very walkable from your Maruyama Park accommodation.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hiroshima (90 min from Kyoto by Shinkansen Nozomi, ~¥10,000 round trip — plan ahead or use a JR Pass if purchased). Visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park and Museum (museum entry ¥200 — one of Japan's most affordable and important museum experiences). The A-Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), a UNESCO World Heritage Site, stands as a powerful reminder of history. This is a deeply moving and historically significant experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry (¥180 one way) from Hiroshima's Ujina Port or Miyajima-guchi to Miyajima Island (Itsukushima). See the iconic 'floating' torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine (¥300 entry) rising from the sea. Explore the island, interact with the friendly deer, and walk through the forested mountain paths. The island has a magical, ancient atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hiroshima city, grab dinner, and take the Shinkansen back to Kyoto. Arrive back by 8:00–9:00 PM.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before departing.
meals.lunch: Miyajima Island — try oysters (kaki), the island's specialty, grilled fresh at waterfront stalls (¥200–¥400 per oyster). Also try momiji manju (maple-leaf-shaped cakes filled with sweet bean paste, ~¥100 each) — a beloved Hiroshima souvenir snack.
meals.dinner: Hiroshima — Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (layered savory pancake with noodles, very different from Osaka style) at Okonomimura — a multi-story building housing 25 okonomiyaki restaurants, all budget-friendly at ¥800–¥1,200 per dish.

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest and most expensive day of the trip due to Shinkansen costs. If budget is very tight, consider skipping Miyajima and spending more time in Hiroshima city, or replacing this day with a second Osaka or Nara visit. The Peace Museum is essential for anyone interested in 20th-century history and is especially impactful for older children and teens. Book Shinkansen tickets in advance for best prices.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Daitoku-ji Temple complex (free grounds, individual sub-temples ¥400–¥600) in northern Kyoto — a vast Zen complex with 24 sub-temples, many featuring exquisite dry landscape gardens. It's far less crowded than the main tourist temples and offers an authentic, contemplative experience. Particularly recommended: Daisen-in and Zuiho-in sub-temples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kitano Tenmangu Shrine (free) — a beautiful Shinto shrine dedicated to the god of learning, with a plum and cherry blossom garden. Nearby, explore the Nishijin textile district, the historic center of Kyoto's silk weaving industry. Visit the Nishijin Ori Kaikan (weaving hall, free admission) to watch live kimono weaving demonstrations and see stunning textiles. Browse the local shopping streets for affordable traditional crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Final proper evening in Kyoto's Gion district. Take a leisurely walk through the preserved machiya streets of Gion Shirakawa — a canal-lined street with weeping cherry trees and traditional tea houses, especially beautiful when lanterns are lit in the evening. Enjoy a final Kyoto dinner at a local favorite.

meals.breakfast: Try a traditional Japanese breakfast at a local cafe or teishoku restaurant — grilled fish, rice, miso soup, pickles, and tamagoyaki (~¥700–¥1,000). A wonderful cultural experience.
meals.lunch: Nishijin area — a local soba noodle shop. Handmade soba (buckwheat noodles) is a Kyoto specialty; a generous set with tempura costs ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last full Kyoto dinner — try a mid-range kaiseki-inspired set dinner at a local restaurant in Gion for ¥2,000–¥3,000. Or keep it budget-friendly with a final izakaya dinner with local sake or beer (~¥1,500).

day_by_day.notes: Daitoku-ji is best reached by bus from Kyoto Station or Shijo (Bus 12 or 204). Nishijin is a 10-minute walk or short bus ride away. The Gion Shirakawa area near your hotel is one of Kyoto's most romantic and photogenic spots — perfect for an evening stroll on your last night. Buy any remaining souvenirs today.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kyoto — wake up early for one last sunrise walk through Maruyama Park to say goodbye to the cherry blossoms. Visit any missed nearby sights: Chion-in Temple (free grounds, ¥500 for inner garden) — one of Japan's largest temple gates (sanmon) is right next to Maruyama Park. Pack your bags and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, take the Haruka Express from Kyoto Station back to Kansai International Airport (75 min, ~¥1,900). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in, security, and immigration. Browse the airport's duty-free shops for last-minute Japanese snacks, cosmetics, and souvenirs at competitive prices.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Kansai International Airport. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Japanese breakfast — grab onigiri, tamagoyaki, and green tea from a convenience store for a nostalgic last meal (~¥400–¥600). Or treat yourself to a sit-down morning set at a Kyoto kissaten.
meals.lunch: Kyoto Station Isetan food hall or a station bento (ekiben) — beautifully packaged Japanese train station lunch boxes are a cultural institution. A Kyoto-style ekiben costs ¥1,000–¥1,500 and makes a wonderful final meal.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Kansai International Airport — the terminal has a good range of restaurants including ramen, sushi conveyor belts, and udon at reasonable prices (¥800–¥1,500).

day_by_day.notes: Kansai International Airport (KIX) is well-served by the Haruka Express from Kyoto Station. Buy your Haruka ticket in advance or use your ICOCA card. Remember to redeem any remaining ICOCA card balance at the airport (machines available at JR ticket offices). Japan has strict customs rules — declare all food items. Consider posting heavy souvenirs home via Japan Post's affordable international parcel service before departure. Total estimated daily budget (excluding Shinkansen on Day 8): ¥4,000–¥7,000 per person per day, covering transport, entry fees, and meals.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activity. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Narita/Haneda Express or Shinkansen toward Kyoto. Journey takes approximately 2.5–3 hours depending on departure airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your Boutique Stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district. Drop your bags, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation stroll through the Gion district — wander Hanamikoji Street, admire the preserved machiya townhouses, and soak in the historic atmosphere at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park — just steps from your hotel, experience your first hanami evening under the iconic weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) at the heart of the park. The tree is beautifully lit up after dark, creating a magical atmosphere. Join locals picnicking beneath the blossoms.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a bento box at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: Pick up an ekiben (station bento box) on the Shinkansen — a classic Japanese travel tradition, around ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Omen Noodle Restaurant near Gion — a beloved local spot serving hearty udon noodles in a warm broth with seasonal vegetables, around ¥1,200–¥1,800 per person

day_by_day.notes: Purchase an IC card (Suica or ICOCA) at the airport for seamless transit and convenience store payments throughout the trip. April 15 is peak cherry blossom season in Kyoto — Maruyama Park will be stunning and lively.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park — start your first full day with a peaceful morning hanami walk through Maruyama Park before the crowds arrive. Visit the adjacent Yasaka Shrine, beautifully framed by cherry blossoms, and explore the quieter northern garden paths.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Higashiyama District — walk the stone-paved Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka lanes lined with traditional shops and tea houses. Visit Kiyomizudera Temple, one of Kyoto's most iconic sites, offering sweeping views of the city framed by cherry blossoms on the hillside.
day_by_day.evening: Gion District evening walk — return through Gion at dusk when lanterns glow and the chances of spotting a maiko (apprentice geisha) are highest. Browse the boutique shops along Shijo Street.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) — toast set with coffee around ¥600–¥900
meals.lunch: Kasagi-ya on Ninenzaka — a historic sweet shop serving matcha and seasonal wagashi (Japanese sweets) alongside light snacks, around ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Gion Kappa — a well-regarded mid-range kaiseki-style restaurant in the Gion area offering seasonal Kyoto cuisine (obanzai), around ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Higashiyama route covers approximately 3–4 km of cobblestone paths. Kiyomizudera has an entry fee of around ¥500. Arrive at the temple by 9:00 AM to beat tour groups.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Tenryu-ji Temple — take the Randen tram or bus to Arashiyama (about 30 minutes from Gion). Walk through the towering bamboo grove early in the morning when light filters through the stalks. Explore the UNESCO-listed Tenryu-ji Temple and its stunning Zen garden with cherry blossoms reflected in the central pond.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Arashiyama — visit the Okochi Sanso Villa garden for panoramic views over the valley, then stroll along the Hozu Riverbank. Stop at Jojakko-ji Temple, a quieter moss-covered gem on the hillside perfect for families.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion and visit Nishiki Market — known as 'Kyoto's Kitchen,' this narrow covered market is perfect for tasting local street foods like pickled vegetables, grilled skewers, and fresh tofu before it closes around 18:00.

meals.breakfast: Grab onigiri and green tea from a convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) near the hotel — quick, delicious, and very affordable at around ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Yoshida-ya in Arashiyama — a charming mid-range restaurant serving tofu kaiseki (yudofu), a Kyoto specialty, around ¥1,800–¥2,500 per person
meals.dinner: Nishiki Market street food crawl — sample tamagoyaki, kushikatsu skewers, fresh yuba (tofu skin), and matcha ice cream for around ¥1,500–¥2,000 total

day_by_day.notes: Tenryu-ji entry fee is approximately ¥500 for the garden, ¥300 additional for the temple building. Arashiyama is very popular on weekends — aim to arrive before 8:30 AM for a quieter bamboo grove experience. The Randen tram is a charming and family-friendly way to travel.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha — take the JR Nara line (about 10 minutes from Kyoto Station) to Fushimi Inari, famous for its thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up the mountain. Hike as far as your family is comfortable — even the first 30 minutes offers spectacular scenery. Early morning light through the gates is breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Nara (30 minutes from Kyoto by JR) — visit Nara Park where hundreds of freely roaming deer bow to visitors. Walk to Todai-ji Temple, housing Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue. A wonderful family-friendly experience combining nature, history, and culture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto and enjoy a relaxed evening near Pontocho Alley — a narrow lantern-lit lane running parallel to the Kamo River, lined with intimate mid-range restaurants. Ideal for a quiet family dinner after a full day.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby bakery — Kyoto has excellent French-Japanese bakeries; try Pain de Kaito near Gion for fresh pastries around ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Edogawa in Nara — a reliable mid-range restaurant near Todai-ji serving set meals (teishoku) of grilled fish, rice, miso soup, and pickles, around ¥1,200–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Pontocho Alley restaurant of choice — look for a restaurant with a riverside terrace (kawayuka) for a memorable evening; budget around ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person for a full meal

day_by_day.notes: Deer crackers (shika senbei) to feed the deer in Nara cost about ¥200 per bundle — kids love this! Be aware that deer can be assertive. Todai-ji entry fee is ¥600. Fushimi Inari is free to enter and open 24 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Kyoto Imperial Palace and Kyoto Gyoen National Garden — the surrounding park is a vast, peaceful green space perfect for a morning walk under cherry blossoms. The Imperial Palace grounds can be explored via a free guided tour (book in advance through the Imperial Household Agency). A wonderful cultural and historical experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-Michi) — walk this beautiful 2 km canal-side path lined with cherry trees from Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion) to Nanzen-ji Temple. Visit Nanzen-ji's impressive Sanmon gate and the surprisingly photogenic red-brick aqueduct running through the temple grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in the Gion area — browse souvenir shops along Shijo-Kawaramachi, pick up local crafts, Kyoto sweets, and ceramics. Enjoy a calm dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at the boutique hotel if offered, or visit Ippodo Tea Co. café near the Imperial Palace for matcha and traditional sweets, around ¥800–¥1,200
meals.lunch: Hinode Udon near Nanzen-ji — a popular local spot serving thick, chewy udon noodles in a rich dashi broth, around ¥900–¥1,400
meals.dinner: Mishima-tei near Shijo — a historic Kyoto restaurant specializing in sukiyaki (hot pot with wagyu beef, tofu, and vegetables cooked tableside), around ¥3,000–¥5,000 per person — a special mid-trip treat

day_by_day.notes: Imperial Palace tours are free but require advance reservation via the Imperial Household Agency website. The Philosopher's Path is at its absolute peak beauty in mid-April. Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion) entry is ¥500 if you wish to enter the garden.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Kyoto to Hiroshima via Shinkansen — the journey takes approximately 1 hour 15 minutes on the Hikari Shinkansen. Arrive in Hiroshima mid-morning and head directly to the Peace Memorial Park area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park — spend a meaningful and deeply moving afternoon at this essential historical site. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, view the iconic A-Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), and explore the museum's thoughtful exhibits documenting the events of August 6, 1945. A profound and important experience for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hiroshima's vibrant Hondori shopping arcade and the lively Nagarekawa entertainment district. Hiroshima is a city of remarkable resilience and warmth — enjoy the local atmosphere before returning to Kyoto.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Kyoto Station before boarding — the station's underground food hall has excellent options including hot sandwiches and pastries, around ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Okonomimura (Okonomiyaki Village) in Hiroshima — a multi-floor building housing dozens of stalls serving Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (savory layered pancake with noodles), a local specialty; around ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Return to Kyoto by evening Shinkansen. Dinner at a restaurant near Kyoto Station — try Kyoto Ramen Koji on the 10th floor of Kyoto Station for excellent regional ramen varieties, around ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum entry fee is ¥200 for adults, ¥50 for children — remarkably affordable for its significance. Allow at least 2 hours inside the museum. This day may be emotionally intense, especially for children — prepare them gently beforehand. Consider purchasing a day-use coin locker at Hiroshima Station to store bags.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Kyoto to Tokyo via Shinkansen — depart Kyoto Station on the Nozomi Shinkansen (approximately 2 hours 15 minutes to Tokyo). Check in to a mid-range hotel in Tokyo (Shinjuku or Asakusa recommended for families). Settle in and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Asakusa and Senso-ji Temple — visit Tokyo's oldest and most famous temple, Senso-ji, approached through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) and the bustling Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks. Explore the surrounding Asakusa district with its rickshaws, kimono rental shops, and old Tokyo atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Tokyo Skytree (adjacent to Asakusa) — visit Japan's tallest structure for panoramic views over the city at dusk and into the evening. The illuminated cityscape stretching to Mount Fuji on clear days is spectacular. A memorable family experience.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at your Kyoto hotel or station before departure
meals.lunch: Nakamise Street snacks in Asakusa — ningyo-yaki (character-shaped cakes), ningyo-yaki, melon bread, and matcha soft serve for a fun, affordable lunch around ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Sometaro in Asakusa — a charming old-fashioned restaurant where you cook your own okonomiyaki at the table; great fun for families, around ¥1,500–¥2,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Skytree tickets cost approximately ¥2,100 for the lower deck (350m) or ¥3,100 for the upper deck (450m) for adults; children's rates are lower. Book online to skip queues. The JR Pass covers the Shinkansen if purchased in advance — highly recommended for this itinerary.

day_by_day.morning: Edo-Tokyo Museum Family Experience — take the JR Sobu line to Ryogoku Station. This spectacular museum features life-size reconstructions of Edo-period streets, bridges, and buildings. Interactive exhibits and scale models bring Japan's history vividly to life — an absolute highlight for families and history enthusiasts alike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ueno Park and Museums — just 15 minutes away by train, Ueno Park may still have late-blooming cherry trees. Visit the Tokyo National Museum (the largest in Japan, housing thousands of cultural artifacts), or opt for the family-friendly Ueno Zoo. The park itself is a lovely place to relax.
day_by_day.evening: Akihabara Electric Town — a short walk or train ride from Ueno, Akihabara dazzles with multi-story electronics shops, anime merchandise, retro game arcades, and maid cafés. A uniquely Tokyo experience, especially fun for families and curious travelers.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby convenience store — Japanese convenience stores (konbini) offer surprisingly excellent hot foods, sandwiches, and coffee for around ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Chanko Nabe restaurant near Ryogoku — the Ryogoku area is home to many sumo stables, and chanko nabe (hearty sumo wrestlers' hot pot stew) is the local specialty; around ¥1,500–¥2,500
meals.dinner: Kanda Yabu Soba near Akihabara — one of Tokyo's most historic soba restaurants, serving hand-cut buckwheat noodles in a beautiful traditional setting since 1880; around ¥1,200–¥2,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Edo-Tokyo Museum entry is approximately ¥600 for adults, free for children under 18. Tokyo National Museum entry is ¥1,000 for adults. Both offer excellent English audio guides. Ryogoku is the sumo district — check if any sumo tournaments (basho) are scheduled during your visit for a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — take the subway to Tsukiji for an immersive morning food experience. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), fresh oysters, grilled scallops, and seasonal street foods. Tsukiji's outer market remains a vibrant hub even after the inner wholesale market relocated. This is breakfast and cultural experience combined.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hamarikyu Gardens (5-minute walk from Tsukiji) — a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with tidal ponds, tea houses, and seasonal flowers set against the backdrop of modern Tokyo skyscrapers. Take a water bus up the Sumida River to Asakusa for a scenic afternoon cruise (around ¥800 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Shibuya and Shinjuku — experience Tokyo's most iconic urban energy. Watch the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing from the Starbucks or Mag's Park viewpoint, then head to Shinjuku's Golden Gai for atmospheric narrow alley bars, or visit the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck for night views over the city.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market food tour — budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person for a satisfying spread of fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and seafood snacks across multiple stalls
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Hamarikyu's traditional tea house — matcha and seasonal wagashi sweets served in a serene garden setting, around ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Ichiran Ramen in Shibuya — the famous solo-booth tonkotsu ramen experience, customizable to your exact taste preferences; around ¥1,200–¥1,500 per person. A uniquely Japanese dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is best visited between 7:00–10:00 AM when produce is freshest and stalls are most active. Hamarikyu Gardens entry is ¥300. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is free and open until 22:30 — one of the best free views in Tokyo.

day_by_day.morning: Meiji Jingu Shrine and Yoyogi Park — start your final day at the serene Meiji Shrine, a forested Shinto sanctuary dedicated to Emperor Meiji, offering a tranquil contrast to Tokyo's urban energy. Walk through the towering torii gate and forested path. Adjacent Yoyogi Park may still have cherry blossoms and is popular with locals on weekends.
day_by_day.afternoon: Harajuku and Omotesando — explore the famous Takeshita Street for colorful Harajuku fashion and quirky crepe shops, then stroll the elegant Omotesando boulevard lined with international boutiques and Japanese designer stores. Visit the Omotesando Hills complex for architecture and shopping. A perfect final afternoon for souvenirs and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Shinjuku — end your 10-day Japan adventure with a memorable dinner. Explore the atmospheric Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane), a tiny alley of smoky yakitori skewer stalls near Shinjuku Station, for an authentic and nostalgic Tokyo send-off. Toast to an incredible trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — take time to enjoy a relaxed final morning meal before heading out
meals.lunch: Harajuku Crepes on Takeshita Street — a Tokyo institution; try strawberry and cream or matcha and red bean crepes for around ¥500–¥700. Supplement with a bowl of ramen from a nearby shop if needed.
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane), Shinjuku — sit elbow-to-elbow at tiny yakitori stalls grilling skewers of chicken, vegetables, and offal over charcoal. Atmospheric, affordable, and quintessentially Tokyo; budget around ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is free to enter and open from sunrise to sunset. If departing tomorrow, begin packing tonight and confirm your airport transfer. Purchase final souvenirs at Omotesando or Shinjuku's department stores (depachika basement food halls are excellent for edible gifts). Keep IC card topped up for easy airport transit.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Japanese tradition of hanami (flower viewing) beneath hundreds of cherry blossom trees, including the famous weeping cherry tree illuminated at night. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the season, and capture breathtaking photos of pink blooms reflected in the park's pond. A quintessential family-friendly cultural experience.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Tokyo's legendary Tsukiji Outer Market and sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, and matcha treats from dozens of street vendors. A fantastic culinary adventure for families to taste authentic Japanese street food culture while wandering vibrant market stalls alongside local chefs and vendors.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: Visit the deeply moving Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and walk through the surrounding Peace Memorial Park, home to the iconic A-Bomb Dome. This profoundly educational experience offers families and history enthusiasts a powerful perspective on World War II and humanity's pursuit of peace. The museum is thoughtfully curated for visitors of all ages.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Tenryu-ji Temple
experiences.description: Walk through the enchanting towering bamboo groves of Arashiyama and explore the UNESCO-listed Tenryu-ji Temple with its stunning traditional Japanese garden featuring cherry blossom trees framing a serene koi pond. Rent a rickshaw for a family-friendly tour of the area and cross the historic Togetsukyo Bridge for panoramic mountain views.

experiences.name: Edo-Tokyo Museum Family Experience
experiences.description: Step back in time at the spectacular Edo-Tokyo Museum, where life-size reconstructions of historic Edo-period streets, bridges, and buildings bring Japanese history vividly to life. Families can interact with exhibits, try on traditional costumes, and learn about samurai culture, merchant life, and the transformation of Tokyo from ancient Edo. Highly engaging for children and adults alike.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00. Clear customs and collect luggage at the airport. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer (black car or limousine service) whisks you directly to your boutique stay in the Gion district near Maruyama Park. Settle in, freshen up, and receive a welcome orientation from the hotel concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle Gion Stroll — After settling in, take a leisurely first walk through the atmospheric Gion district. Wander the iconic Hanamikoji Street lined with traditional ochaya (tea houses) and admire the preserved machiya townhouses. If timing allows, catch an early glimpse of geiko or maiko heading to evening appointments — a quintessential Kyoto moment.
day_by_day.evening: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park — Just steps from your hotel, experience the magical tradition of hanami beneath Maruyama Park's legendary weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura), beautifully illuminated after dusk. Mid-April is peak bloom season, making this a truly spectacular welcome to Japan. Stroll the lantern-lit paths at a relaxed pace.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a meal on the plane or a light snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a quick premium bento from an airport lounge or convenience store en route — save appetite for dinner.
meals.dinner: Mizai (Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurant in Kyoto) — An exquisite multi-course kaiseki dinner celebrating seasonal spring ingredients. Alternatively, Kikunoi Honten, a legendary three-Michelin-star kaiseki institution a short walk from your hotel, offering a curated tasting menu with sake pairings.

day_by_day.notes: April 15 typically falls within peak cherry blossom season in Kyoto. Book kaiseki dinner well in advance — Kikunoi and Mizai require reservations months ahead. Request a room with a garden or park-facing view at check-in. The hotel concierge can arrange a private hanami picnic set with premium sake and seasonal sweets for your evening in Maruyama Park.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Tenryu-ji Temple — Depart early by private car to Arashiyama (approx. 30 minutes from Gion) to beat the crowds. Walk through the towering, otherworldly bamboo groves as morning light filters through the stalks. Then explore the UNESCO World Heritage Tenryu-ji Temple and its stunning Sogenchi Garden, one of Japan's finest strolling gardens with a backdrop of Arashiyama mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arashiyama Exploration — After the temple, visit the serene Jojakko-ji or Okochi Sanso Villa (the garden estate of a silent-film actor) for panoramic views over Kyoto. Return to Gion by private car in the early afternoon. Rest briefly, then visit Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') for a curated tasting walk of premium pickles, matcha sweets, and seasonal delicacies.
day_by_day.evening: Gion Corner Cultural Experience — Attend an exclusive performance at Gion Corner showcasing traditional Japanese arts including maiko dance, koto music, ikebana, and tea ceremony. Afterward, explore the lantern-lit back alleys of Gion Shirakawa along the canal — one of Japan's most romantic evening scenes.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel premium Japanese breakfast featuring grilled fish, dashi egg, miso soup, pickles, and seasonal rice — a quintessential ryokan-style morning spread.
meals.lunch: Shigetsu at Tenryu-ji — A rare opportunity to dine on shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) inside the temple grounds, with views over the Sogenchi Garden. Reserve in advance.
meals.dinner: Nakamura (est. 1716) — One of Kyoto's oldest and most prestigious kaiseki restaurants near Nishiki Market, serving refined Kyoto cuisine with centuries of heritage. Private tatami room dining available.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Arashiyama Bamboo Grove before 8:00 AM for a near-private experience — your hotel concierge can arrange an early private car. Tenryu-ji garden entry is separate from the temple building; both are worth visiting. Book Shigetsu lunch at Tenryu-ji directly through the temple's reservation system.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine — Private car to Fushimi Inari (20 minutes south of Gion). Begin the hike through the iconic thousands of vermillion torii gates at dawn or early morning when the path is serene. Hike as far as Yotsutsuji intersection for panoramic views over Kyoto, then descend. A private guided tour can illuminate the Shinto significance and hidden sub-shrines along the trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nijo Castle and Kyoto Imperial Palace — Visit Nijo Castle, the opulent Edo-period shogun residence with its famous 'nightingale floors' and stunning Ninomaru Palace interiors. Follow with a guided stroll through the Kyoto Imperial Palace Park, with optional interior access via advance reservation through the Imperial Household Agency.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Machiya Dinner Experience — Return to Gion for an exclusive private dinner hosted inside a restored 200-year-old machiya townhouse. Many luxury operators (such as Kyoto Cuisine & Maiko Evening) offer private dining with a maiko performance, sake tasting, and seasonal Kyoto cuisine — a once-in-a-lifetime cultural immersion.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departing — fresh fruit, yogurt, and matcha before the Fushimi hike.
meals.lunch: Tofuya Ukai Kyoto — A premium tofu kaiseki restaurant set in a traditional garden near Fushimi, celebrating Kyoto's legendary silken tofu cuisine in an exquisite setting.
meals.dinner: Private machiya dining experience with maiko entertainment — curated by your hotel concierge. Dishes feature seasonal Kyoto-style cuisine (obanzai) with premium sake and local craft beverages.

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free to enter and open 24 hours — arriving at 6:30–7:00 AM is ideal on a Saturday to avoid crowds. Nijo Castle requires advance tickets; book online. The maiko dining experience must be booked weeks in advance through specialist operators such as Gion Hatanaka or Peter Macintosh's Gion experience.

day_by_day.morning: Philosopher's Path & Higashiyama Temple Walk — Stroll the cherry-blossom-lined Philosopher's Path canal walk (Tetsugaku-no-Michi) from Nanzenji to Ginkakuji (Silver Pavilion). In April, this is one of Japan's most beautiful hanami walks. Visit Nanzenji Temple's grand Sanmon gate and aqueduct, then continue north past Eikan-do to the moss garden of Ginkakuji.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kinkakuji (Golden Pavilion) & Ryoanji — Private car to northwest Kyoto. Visit the dazzling gold-leaf-covered Kinkakuji reflected in its mirror pond, then continue to Ryoanji Temple for contemplative time before Japan's most famous Zen rock garden — a UNESCO World Heritage site. End with a visit to Ninnaji Temple's cherry-blossom orchard (late-blooming omuro cherry trees often peak in mid-April).
day_by_day.evening: Sake Tasting & Kaiseki Dinner — Begin the evening with a private premium sake tasting session arranged by your concierge at a renowned Kyoto sake specialist. Follow with dinner at Hyotei, a three-Michelin-star restaurant with 450 years of history, celebrated for its morning kaiseki and seasonal tasting menus.

meals.breakfast: Full Japanese breakfast at the hotel — seasonal grilled fish, tofu, pickled vegetables, miso soup, and premium green tea.
meals.lunch: Omen Noodle Restaurant near Ginkakuji — a beloved artisan udon restaurant with a cozy atmosphere, perfect for a warm bowl after the Philosopher's Path walk. Or opt for a premium bento enjoyed on the canal path itself.
meals.dinner: Hyotei — Three Michelin stars, 450-year legacy. Reserve the multi-course kaiseki tasting menu with sake pairing. Private rooms available.

day_by_day.notes: The Philosopher's Path is best walked Sunday morning before tourist crowds peak. Ninnaji's omuro cherry trees are a hidden gem that often bloom later than other varieties — confirm bloom status with your concierge closer to the date. Hyotei requires reservations months in advance; your hotel concierge should assist.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Nara — Private car or luxury coach to Nara (45 minutes from Kyoto). Explore Nara Park and feed the famously friendly free-roaming sika deer. Visit the awe-inspiring Todai-ji Temple, home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue (Daibutsu). Continue to the atmospheric Kasuga Taisha Shrine, lined with thousands of stone and bronze lanterns draped in moss.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nara Continued — Visit Isuien Garden, one of Japan's finest Meiji-era strolling gardens with borrowed scenery of Todai-ji and Wakakusa Hill. Then explore the traditional preserved merchant district of Naramachi, browsing artisan craft shops and lacquerware galleries. Return to Kyoto by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed Evening in Gion — After a full day in Nara, enjoy a gentle evening. Visit the beautiful Yasaka Shrine (free entry, open 24 hours) adjacent to Maruyama Park, beautifully lit at night. Indulge in a traditional onsen bath if your boutique hotel has private bathing facilities, or arrange a private onsen session.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — premium Japanese set with seasonal ingredients.
meals.lunch: Yoshikawa Nara — A refined kaiseki lunch restaurant in Nara serving seasonal cuisine in a traditional setting, steps from Naramachi.
meals.dinner: Mizuki at The Sodoh Higashiyama — An elegant restaurant in a restored early 20th-century villa in the Higashiyama hills, offering refined Japanese cuisine in a garden setting. Lighter menu ideal after a full travel day.

day_by_day.notes: Deer in Nara Park are wild animals — they can be assertive around food. Deer crackers (shika senbei) are sold throughout the park for feeding. Todai-ji is busiest midday; aim to arrive at opening (8:00 AM) for a more peaceful experience. A private guide for Nara is highly recommended to unlock the historical depth of the temples.

day_by_day.morning: Shinkansen to Tokyo — Check out of Kyoto boutique stay and transfer by private car to Kyoto Station. Board the Nozomi Shinkansen bullet train to Tokyo (approx. 2 hours 15 minutes). Book Green Car (first class) seats for a premium experience with Mt. Fuji views on clear days (right side of train heading to Tokyo). Arrive at Tokyo Station and transfer to your luxury Tokyo hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Edo-Tokyo Museum Family Experience — After checking in, head to the spectacular Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku. Explore life-size reconstructions of Edo-period streets, replica merchant shops, kabuki theaters, and interactive exhibits tracing Tokyo's transformation from feudal city to modern metropolis. This is an outstanding experience for all ages, bringing Japanese history vividly to life.
day_by_day.evening: Asakusa & Senso-ji Temple by Night — Travel to Asakusa and explore the iconic Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest temple, dramatically illuminated after dark. Walk Nakamise-dori shopping street for premium craft souvenirs, then enjoy the atmospheric Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) area. The nearby Sumida River offers beautiful views of Tokyo Skytree reflected in the water.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at hotel or a premium ekiben (train station bento) purchased at Kyoto Station — Kyoto ekiben are renowned for their quality and presentation.
meals.lunch: Chanko Nabe lunch in Ryogoku — the traditional protein-rich hot pot of sumo wrestlers, served at authentic chanko restaurants surrounding the Ryogoku Kokugikan sumo arena, adjacent to the Edo-Tokyo Museum.
meals.dinner: Imahan Honten in Asakusa — A legendary sukiyaki and shabu-shabu restaurant established in 1895, celebrated for premium Wagyu beef. Private tatami rooms available for an intimate family dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Book Green Car Shinkansen seats well in advance, especially during spring travel season. The Edo-Tokyo Museum has English audio guides and interactive displays ideal for families. Confirm Tokyo luxury hotel booking — options such as Aman Tokyo, The Peninsula Tokyo, or Mandarin Oriental are recommended for this itinerary's premium standard.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Begin the day with an early private guided food tour of the legendary Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample the finest fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, premium matcha, and seasonal street foods. Visit specialty vendors for premium dashi, pickles, and Japanese knives. A private guide maximizes the experience and navigates the best stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hamarikyu Gardens & Tokyo Bay — Walk to the adjacent Hamarikyu Gardens, a stunning Edo-period feudal garden with tidal ponds, tea pavilions, and cherry blossom trees. Enjoy a traditional matcha and wagashi (Japanese sweet) ceremony in the garden's Nakajima no Ochaya teahouse on the pond. Afterward, take a scenic water bus along the Sumida River to Asakusa for a relaxed afternoon stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Ginza Luxury District & Fine Dining — Explore the prestigious Ginza district — Tokyo's equivalent of the Champs-Élysées — browsing flagship stores of Japanese artisan brands (Mikimoto pearls, Itoya stationery, premium department stores). End the evening with dinner at one of Tokyo's most celebrated restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — the tour itself serves as a progressive breakfast of premium market bites: uni (sea urchin), otoro (fatty tuna) sushi, tamagoyaki, and fresh oysters.
meals.lunch: Sushi Saito or Sushi Yoshitake (Michelin three-star) in Ginza — reserve months in advance for an omakase counter experience with Tokyo's finest sushi masters. Alternatively, Kyubey Ginza for a legendary sushi omakase in an accessible luxury setting.
meals.dinner: Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (Ginza) — The world-famous three-Michelin-star sushi restaurant of Jiro Ono, immortalized in 'Jiro Dreams of Sushi.' Reservations are extraordinarily difficult; your hotel concierge must assist. Alternatively, Quintessence (three Michelin stars, French-Japanese fusion in Shinagawa) for a different culinary dimension.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is best visited 7:00–9:00 AM when vendors are freshest and most active. A private guide (available through luxury operators like Magical Trip or Japan Travel) transforms the experience. Hamarikyu teahouse charges a small fee for matcha service — worth every yen for the garden setting. Top-tier sushi reservations in Tokyo require months of advance planning.

day_by_day.morning: Meiji Jingu Shrine & Harajuku — Begin with a serene early morning visit to Meiji Jingu Shrine, Tokyo's most important Shinto shrine, set within a 170-acre forested sanctuary in the heart of the city. Walk the grand gravel path through towering cedar trees to the main shrine complex. Witness morning rituals if timing aligns. Then explore the adjacent Yoyogi Park, a popular hanami spot, for any remaining cherry blossoms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Omotesando & Nezu Museum — Stroll the elegant Omotesando boulevard (Tokyo's most architecturally sophisticated shopping street) past flagship buildings designed by world-renowned architects (Tadao Ando, Kengo Kuma, Toyo Ito). Visit the exceptional Nezu Museum, housing a world-class collection of pre-modern Asian art in a stunning garden setting with a traditional teahouse. The bamboo-lined garden path is a hidden urban oasis.
day_by_day.evening: Shibuya & Tokyo Tower — Experience the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing from the Shibuya Sky observation deck for a bird's-eye perspective. Then travel to Tokyo Tower for evening illumination views. End the night in the upscale Azabu-Juban or Roppongi Hills area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — premium buffet or à la carte at your luxury Tokyo hotel's restaurant.
meals.lunch: Omotesando Hills or Aoyama — dine at a premium restaurant in this fashionable district. Recommend: Maisen (legendary premium katsu sandwiches) for a casual luxury lunch, or Florilège (two Michelin stars, innovative French-Japanese) for a sophisticated midday experience.
meals.dinner: Ryugin — Three Michelin stars in Roppongi, Chef Seiji Yamamoto's celebrated kaiseki restaurant pushing the boundaries of Japanese cuisine with avant-garde techniques and seasonal ingredients. One of Asia's most acclaimed dining destinations.

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is most peaceful before 8:00 AM. The forest path is meditative and beautiful even outside cherry blossom season. Nezu Museum requires a timed entry ticket — book online in advance. The Shibuya Sky observation deck requires advance online booking; sunset time slots sell out weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Nikko Day Trip — Board a private car or luxury coach to Nikko (approximately 2 hours from Tokyo). Visit the extraordinarily ornate Toshogu Shrine complex — the mausoleum of Tokugawa Ieyasu, Japan's first shogun — a UNESCO World Heritage Site dripping in gold leaf, lacquerwork, and intricate wood carvings. Explore the surrounding Rinnoji Temple and Futarasan Shrine within the cedar forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nikko Continued — Walk to Shinkyo Bridge, the sacred vermillion lacquer bridge over the Daiya River, and explore the Kanmangafuchi Abyss — a mysterious gorge lined with dozens of moss-covered Jizo statues. If time allows, visit Kegon Falls, one of Japan's most spectacular waterfalls, a short drive from central Nikko. Return to Tokyo by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Luxury Evening in Tokyo — Return to your hotel to refresh, then enjoy a final premium Tokyo evening. Visit the Park Hyatt Tokyo's New York Bar (made famous by 'Lost in Translation') on the 52nd floor for cocktails with panoramic city views, before a final celebratory dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early light hotel breakfast before departure to Nikko.
meals.lunch: Meiji-no-Yakata in Nikko — A historic Western-style restaurant set in a 19th-century villa once used by foreign diplomats, serving classic European cuisine that has been a Nikko institution for over a century.
meals.dinner: New York Grill at Park Hyatt Tokyo (Shinjuku) — A legendary Tokyo fine dining institution on the 52nd floor with sweeping city views, serving premium steaks, fresh seafood, and an exceptional wine list. The perfect celebratory final dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Nikko is approximately 2 hours from Tokyo by private car or 1 hour 45 minutes by Tobu Limited Express train from Asakusa. A private guide for Nikko is strongly recommended — the historical and religious complexity of Toshogu rewards deep explanation. Book New York Grill dinner well in advance, particularly on a Friday evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final Tokyo Morning — Enjoy a leisurely final morning in Tokyo. Take a peaceful stroll through the East Gardens of the Imperial Palace (open Tuesday–Sunday, free entry), one of Tokyo's most serene green spaces with beautiful spring plantings. Browse the Marunouchi and Nihonbashi districts for last-minute premium souvenirs: Nihonbashi Takashimaya department store offers the finest Japanese crafts, lacquerware, ceramics, and food gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium Shopping & Departure Preparation — Visit Coredo Muromachi in Nihonbashi for curated Japanese artisan goods, or the Japan Folk Crafts Museum in Komaba for museum-quality mingei (folk art) pieces. Return to hotel, collect luggage, and arrange private luxury transfer to the airport. Allow ample time for international departure procedures.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — Proceed to the airport for your international departure flight. Enjoy the premium airport lounge facilities before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final premium hotel breakfast — savor a full Japanese or Western breakfast at your leisure, a fitting conclusion to ten days of extraordinary Japanese cuisine.
meals.lunch: Nihonbashi Yukari — A three-Michelin-star kaiseki restaurant in the historic Nihonbashi district, perfect for a final celebratory lunch showcasing the very best of Japanese seasonal cuisine before departure.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an in-flight premium meal — many international first-class lounges at Narita and Haneda offer exceptional Japanese food options prepared by renowned chefs.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–3.5 hours before international departure for check-in, security, and customs at Narita or Haneda. If flying from Haneda, the airport is significantly closer to central Tokyo (30–40 minutes by private car). Ask your hotel concierge to arrange luggage forwarding (takuhaibin) to the airport the evening before if you wish to travel light on your final morning. Consider purchasing premium Japanese food gifts at Nihonbashi Takashimaya's basement food hall — an extraordinary selection of the finest Japanese confections, teas, and preserved foods.
